tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

1	# Feature Specification: P-F000 — Foundation
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `001-foundation` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-11
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-F000 — Foundation: Build the foundation that every later unit uses (project scaffold, design tokens, HTTP client with Either/Failure error mapping, login/sign-up, splash, base navigation, expired-session overlay), as described in docs/input/requirements.md section 12, without implementing RF01–RF10, hardcoding visual values outside design_tokens.dart, or changing the backend."
10	
11	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
12	
13	### User Story 1 - Returning user logs in (Priority: P1)
14	
15	A person who already has a Cerne account opens the app, enters their email and password on the login screen, and reaches the main conversation screen (Home/Chat).
16	
17	**Why this priority**: Nothing else in the product — capture, chat, records, settings — is reachable without this. It is the single gate every other unit depends on.
18	
19	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by submitting valid credentials on the login screen and confirming the app lands on Home/Chat; delivers a working, demonstrable access path on its own.
20	
21	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
22	
23	1. **Given** a user with a valid existing account and no active session, **When** they enter the correct email and password on the login screen and submit, **Then** they are authenticated and taken to the Home/Chat screen.
24	2. **Given** a user on the login screen, **When** they submit incorrect credentials, **Then** they see a clear, non-crashing error message and remain on the login screen able to retry.
25	3. **Given** a user with no network connection, **When** they submit the login form, **Then** they see a retryable connection-error message rather than the app hanging or crashing.
26	
27	---
28	
29	### User Story 2 - New user creates an account (Priority: P2)
30	
31	A person without a Cerne account switches the same screen to sign-up mode, enters an email and password, and reaches Home/Chat as a newly created user.
32	
33	**Why this priority**: Required for anyone without an account to enter the product at all, but it depends on the same screen and session machinery as login, so it is one step below it.
34	
35	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by toggling to "Criar conta", submitting a new email/password pair, and confirming an account is created and the app lands on Home/Chat.
36	
37	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
38	
39	1. **Given** a person without an account, **When** they switch to "Criar conta" mode, enter a new email and password, and submit, **Then** an account is created and they are taken directly to Home/Chat.
40	2. **Given** a person entering an email that is already registered, **When** they submit the sign-up form, **Then** they see a clear error message and can correct and retry without the app crashing.
41	
42	---
43	
44	### User Story 3 - App launches and routes by session state (Priority: P3)
45	
46	Whenever the app is opened, it shows a brief splash state, checks whether a usable session already exists, and sends the user straight to Home/Chat or to the login/sign-up screen accordingly — without ever leaving them stuck on the splash screen.
47	
48	**Why this priority**: Determines where every single app session begins; it depends on User Story 1 existing but is a thin routing layer on top of it rather than new user-facing capability.
49	
50	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by launching the app under three stored-session conditions (valid, expired-but-refreshable, none) and confirming the correct landing screen each time.
51	
52	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
53	
54	1. **Given** a device with a previously stored, still-valid session, **When** the app is launched, **Then** after the splash state the user lands directly on Home/Chat without re-entering credentials.
55	2. **Given** a device with no stored session (first launch, or after logout), **When** the app is launched, **Then** after the splash state the user lands on the login/sign-up screen.
56	3. **Given** a device with an expired-but-refreshable session, **When** the app is launched, **Then** the app renews the session in the background and lands on Home/Chat without prompting the user.
57	
58	---
59	
60	### User Story 4 - Navigating between the main screens (Priority: P4)
61	
62	From Home/Chat, the user opens the side menu and moves to Meus Registros or Configurações (today, placeholders), and back, without losing their place.
63	
64	**Why this priority**: Establishes the skeleton every later unit (RF06/RF07/RF05, RF09, etc.) will fill in; it has no functional payload yet, so it ranks below the screens that actually unlock product value.
65	
66	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the side menu from Home/Chat, visiting each destination, and returning, confirming Home/Chat's state is unchanged.
67	
68	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
69	
70	1. **Given** the user is on Home/Chat, **When** they open the side menu and select "Meus Registros", **Then** they see the Meus Registros placeholder screen and can return to Home/Chat.
71	2. **Given** the user is on Home/Chat, **When** they open the side menu and select "Configurações", **Then** they see the Configurações placeholder screen and can return to Home/Chat.
72	3. **Given** the user is on any main screen, **When** they open the side menu, **Then** the menu overlays the current screen without discarding the state underneath it.
73	
74	---
75	
76	### User Story 5 - Session expires during active use (Priority: P5)
77	
78	While the user is actively on a screen (e.g., scrolled partway through Home/Chat), the backend session expires; an overlay appears explaining this and offering to log in again, and once they do, they return to exactly where they were.
79	
80	**Why this priority**: An edge condition of an already-working session (Story 1); important for trust and data safety, but it cannot be exercised until login and at least one screen exist.
81	
82	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a session-expired response while a screen is in a known state, confirming the overlay appears over it unchanged, and confirming re-authentication restores that exact state.
83	
84	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
85	
86	1. **Given** the user is actively viewing a screen in a particular state (e.g., a given scroll position), **When** the backend reports the session has expired, **Then** a "Sessão expirada" overlay appears on top of the current screen without resetting its state.
87	2. **Given** the "Sessão expirada" overlay is visible, **When** the user taps "Entrar novamente" and re-authenticates successfully, **Then** the overlay is dismissed and the underlying screen is restored exactly as it was.
88	
89	---
90	
91	### Edge Cases
92	
93	- Submitting the login or sign-up form with an empty field shows an inline validation message immediately, with no network call made.
94	- The backend rejects a login or sign-up submission as malformed (non-retryable) — this is shown and handled distinctly from a timeout or offline condition (retryable).
95	- The stored access token is present but its refresh token is itself invalid or expired at launch — the user is routed to the login screen, never left stuck on the splash state.
96	- The session expires a second time while the user is still dismissing a "Sessão expirada" overlay from the first expiration — the overlay persists/reappears rather than letting the user proceed with a stale session.
97	- A user opens a placeholder screen (Meus Registros, Configurações) before its owning unit is built — it renders cleanly as "not yet available" rather than a blank or broken screen.
98	- The app is backgrounded mid-submission of login or sign-up — on resume, the request either completes normally or fails cleanly, and never results in a duplicate account or a duplicate session.
99	
100	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
101	
102	### Functional Requirements
103	
104	- **FR-001**: The project MUST be organized so that every feature added from this unit onward follows one fixed folder convention, so later units have a single place to add their own code without restructuring the foundation.
105	- **FR-002**: The system MUST define every visual value (color, typography, spacing, corner radius) used anywhere in the app in exactly one central place; no screen delivered by this unit may define a visual value anywhere else.
106	- **FR-003**: The system MUST provide a single way for any feature to call the backend that always yields either a success result or a typed failure — never an unhandled crash.
107	- **FR-004**: The system MUST translate every backend error response's error code, message, and retryable flag into a failure the UI can act on, so screens can tell a retryable problem (e.g., timeout) from one that is not (e.g., invalid credentials).
108	- **FR-005**: The system MUST address the backend using the documented real request path for each operation, not the contract's documentation-only path.
109	- **FR-006**: Users MUST be able to create a new account by submitting an email and password from the sign-up mode of the login screen.
110	- **FR-007**: Users MUST be able to authenticate with an existing email and password from the login mode of the same screen.
111	- **FR-008**: Users MUST be able to toggle between login and sign-up mode on the same screen without being sent to a different screen.
112	- **FR-009**: The system MUST check, on every app launch, whether a usable session already exists — renewing it first if it is merely expired-but-renewable — and route the user to Home/Chat when one exists or to the login screen otherwise.
113	- **FR-010**: The system MUST show a splash state while this session check (and any related background preparation) is in progress, before routing the user anywhere.
114	- **FR-011**: Users MUST be able to reach Home/Chat, Meus Registros, and Configurações from a side menu, and return to Home/Chat from either of them.
115	- **FR-012**: Meus Registros and Configurações MUST appear as clearly-labeled placeholder screens with no functional behavior from later requirements (RF01–RF10), reserving space for the units that will fill them in.
116	- **FR-013**: The system MUST show a "Sessão expirada" overlay on top of whatever screen the user is on when the backend reports the session has expired, without discarding that screen's state underneath.
117	- **FR-014**: Users MUST be able to dismiss the "Sessão expirada" overlay by re-authenticating, after which the screen underneath MUST be restored to its prior state.
118	- **FR-015**: The system MUST present a clear, non-crashing message for every error condition that sign-up, login, session-renewal, or session-check can return.
119	- **FR-016**: This unit MUST NOT implement the functional behavior of any RF01–RF10 requirement; any screen or control belonging to one of them MUST exist only as an inert placeholder, if at all.
120	- **FR-017**: This unit MUST NOT modify the backend, its contract, or its configuration in any way.
121	
122	### Key Entities
123	
124	- **Session**: Represents whether the user is currently authenticated — holds the information needed to stay logged in and to know when it has expired or can be silently renewed. Determines whether a launch routes to Home/Chat or to the login screen, and whether an active screen receives the "Sessão expirada" overlay.
125	- **Account**: The identity a person signs up with or logs into — an email address and the credential tied to it.
126	- **Backend Failure**: The error outcome every call introduced by this unit (sign-up, login, refresh, session check) can produce — carries enough information to distinguish a retryable problem from a non-retryable one, and to choose the message shown to the user.
127	- **Placeholder Destination**: A navigable screen (Meus Registros, Configurações) that exists so later units have somewhere to add their functionality, but carries no behavior of its own in this unit.
128	
129	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
130	
131	### Measurable Outcomes
132	
133	- **SC-001**: 100% of returning users with a valid stored session reach Home/Chat automatically after the splash state, with no login step required.
134	- **SC-002**: A new user can go from the sign-up form to a usable Home/Chat screen in a single successful attempt, with no intermediate screen other than the brief splash state.
135	- **SC-003**: Every error condition that sign-up, login, session-renewal, and session-check can return produces a readable on-screen message rather than a blank screen, a crash, or an indefinite loading state.
136	- **SC-004**: A user can reach each of the main screens (Home/Chat, Meus Registros, Configurações) from the side menu, and return to Home/Chat, in 2 taps or fewer, every time.
137	- **SC-005**: When a session expires while a screen is in a particular state, that same state (e.g., scroll position, visible content) is unchanged after the user re-authenticates, in every observed case.
138	- **SC-006**: Every screen delivered by this unit visually matches the prototype's documented colors, typography, and spacing, with zero visual values defined outside the single central source.
139	
140	## Assumptions
141	
142	- Biometric/PIN authentication (RF03) is its own delivery unit, built immediately after this one. Until it exists, the splash state routes directly between itself and the login/sign-up screen — the biometric step shown in the prototype's navigation map is intentionally skipped for this unit and will be inserted by the RF03 unit.
143	- Re-authenticating from the "Sessão expirada" overlay goes to the login screen (not to a biometric step), for the same reason — RF03 is not yet part of the app.
144	- Sign-up collects only an email and a password, matching both the prototype (which shows no additional fields) and the backend's sign-up contract.
145	- Session renewal is attempted silently in the background whenever a request fails because the session has merely expired; the "Sessão expirada" overlay is shown only once silent renewal itself is not possible.
146	- Where this unit's side menu is shown, "Planos de Ação" may exist as an inert placeholder entry per the product's extension-feature policy, but is not required navigation for this unit — only Home/Chat, Meus Registros, and Configurações are.
147	- Access and refresh tokens are kept on the device between app launches so a returning user is not asked to log in every time; the specific on-device storage mechanism is an implementation choice, not fixed by this specification.
148	- Every error this unit's calls (sign-up, login, refresh, session check) can return is one of the backend's fixed, documented error codes; no other error shape is expected from these calls.
149

A person who already has a Cerne account opens the app, enters their email and password on the login screen, and reaches the main conversation screen (Home/Chat).

**Why this priority**: Nothing else in the product — capture, chat, records, settings — is reachable without this. It is the single gate every other unit depends on.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by submitting valid credentials on the login screen and confirming the app lands on Home/Chat; delivers a working, demonstrable access path on its own.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a user with a valid existing account and no active session, **When** they enter the correct email and password on the login screen and submit, **Then** they are authenticated and taken to the Home/Chat screen.
2. **Given** a user on the login screen, **When** they submit incorrect credentials, **Then** they see a clear, non-crashing error message and remain on the login screen able to retry.
3. **Given** a user with no network connection, **When** they submit the login form, **Then** they see a retryable connection-error message rather than the app hanging or crashing.

---

### User Story 2 - New user creates an account (Priority: P2)

A person without a Cerne account switches the same screen to sign-up mode, enters an email and password, and reaches Home/Chat as a newly created user.

**Why this priority**: Required for anyone without an account to enter the product at all, but it depends on the same screen and session machinery as login, so it is one step below it.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by toggling to "Criar conta", submitting a new email/password pair, and confirming an account is created and the app lands on Home/Chat.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a person without an account, **When** they switch to "Criar conta" mode, enter a new email and password, and submit, **Then** an account is created and they are taken directly to Home/Chat.
2. **Given** a person entering an email that is already registered, **When** they submit the sign-up form, **Then** they see a clear error message and can correct and retry without the app crashing.

---

### User Story 3 - App launches and routes by session state (Priority: P3)

Whenever the app is opened, it shows a brief splash state, checks whether a usable session already exists, and sends the user straight to Home/Chat or to the login/sign-up screen accordingly — without ever leaving them stuck on the splash screen.

**Why this priority**: Determines where every single app session begins; it depends on User Story 1 existing but is a thin routing layer on top of it rather than new user-facing capability.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by launching the app under three stored-session conditions (valid, expired-but-refreshable, none) and confirming the correct landing screen each time.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a device with a previously stored, still-valid session, **When** the app is launched, **Then** after the splash state the user lands directly on Home/Chat without re-entering credentials.
2. **Given** a device with no stored session (first launch, or after logout), **When** the app is launched, **Then** after the splash state the user lands on the login/sign-up screen.
3. **Given** a device with an expired-but-refreshable session, **When** the app is launched, **Then** the app renews the session in the background and lands on Home/Chat without prompting the user.

---

### User Story 4 - Navigating between the main screens (Priority: P4)

From Home/Chat, the user opens the side menu and moves to Meus Registros or Configurações (today, placeholders), and back, without losing their place.

**Why this priority**: Establishes the skeleton every later unit (RF06/RF07/RF05, RF09, etc.) will fill in; it has no functional payload yet, so it ranks below the screens that actually unlock product value.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the side menu from Home/Chat, visiting each destination, and returning, confirming Home/Chat's state is unchanged.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is on Home/Chat, **When** they open the side menu and select "Meus Registros", **Then** they see the Meus Registros placeholder screen and can return to Home/Chat.
2. **Given** the user is on Home/Chat, **When** they open the side menu and select "Configurações", **Then** they see the Configurações placeholder screen and can return to Home/Chat.
3. **Given** the user is on any main screen, **When** they open the side menu, **Then** the menu overlays the current screen without discarding the state underneath it.

---

### User Story 5 - Session expires during active use (Priority: P5)

While the user is actively on a screen (e.g., scrolled partway through Home/Chat), the backend session expires; an overlay appears explaining this and offering to log in again, and once they do, they return to exactly where they were.

**Why this priority**: An edge condition of an already-working session (Story 1); important for trust and data safety, but it cannot be exercised until login and at least one screen exist.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a session-expired response while a screen is in a known state, confirming the overlay appears over it unchanged, and confirming re-authentication restores that exact state.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is actively viewing a screen in a particular state (e.g., a given scroll position), **When** the backend reports the session has expired, **Then** a "Sessão expirada" overlay appears on top of the current screen without resetting its state.
2. **Given** the "Sessão expirada" overlay is visible, **When** the user taps "Entrar novamente" and re-authenticates successfully, **Then** the overlay is dismissed and the underlying screen is restored exactly as it was.

---

### Edge Cases

- Submitting the login or sign-up form with an empty field shows an inline validation message immediately, with no network call made.
- The backend rejects a login or sign-up submission as malformed (non-retryable) — this is shown and handled distinctly from a timeout or offline condition (retryable).
- The stored access token is present but its refresh token is itself invalid or expired at launch — the user is routed to the login screen, never left stuck on the splash state.
- The session expires a second time while the user is still dismissing a "Sessão expirada" overlay from the first expiration — the overlay persists/reappears rather than letting the user proceed with a stale session.
- A user opens a placeholder screen (Meus Registros, Configurações) before its owning unit is built — it renders cleanly as "not yet available" rather than a blank or broken screen.
- The app is backgrounded mid-submission of login or sign-up — on resume, the request either completes normally or fails cleanly, and never results in a duplicate account or a duplicate session.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The project MUST be organized so that every feature added from this unit onward follows one fixed folder convention, so later units have a single place to add their own code without restructuring the foundation.
- **FR-002**: The system MUST define every visual value (color, typography, spacing, corner radius) used anywhere in the app in exactly one central place; no screen delivered by this unit may define a visual value anywhere else.
- **FR-003**: The system MUST provide a single way for any feature to call the backend that always yields either a success result or a typed failure — never an unhandled crash.
- **FR-004**: The system MUST translate every backend error response's error code, message, and retryable flag into a failure the UI can act on, so screens can tell a retryable problem (e.g., timeout) from one that is not (e.g., invalid credentials).
- **FR-005**: The system MUST address the backend using the documented real request path for each operation, not the contract's documentation-only path.
- **FR-006**: Users MUST be able to create a new account by submitting an email and password from the sign-up mode of the login screen.
- **FR-007**: Users MUST be able to authenticate with an existing email and password from the login mode of the same screen.
- **FR-008**: Users MUST be able to toggle between login and sign-up mode on the same screen without being sent to a different screen.
- **FR-009**: The system MUST check, on every app launch, whether a usable session already exists — renewing it first if it is merely expired-but-renewable — and route the user to Home/Chat when one exists or to the login screen otherwise.
- **FR-010**: The system MUST show a splash state while this session check (and any related background preparation) is in progress, before routing the user anywhere.
- **FR-011**: Users MUST be able to reach Home/Chat, Meus Registros, and Configurações from a side menu, and return to Home/Chat from either of them.
- **FR-012**: Meus Registros and Configurações MUST appear as clearly-labeled placeholder screens with no functional behavior from later requirements (RF01–RF10), reserving space for the units that will fill them in.
- **FR-013**: The system MUST show a "Sessão expirada" overlay on top of whatever screen the user is on when the backend reports the session has expired, without discarding that screen's state underneath.
- **FR-014**: Users MUST be able to dismiss the "Sessão expirada" overlay by re-authenticating, after which the screen underneath MUST be restored to its prior state.
- **FR-015**: The system MUST present a clear, non-crashing message for every error condition that sign-up, login, session-renewal, or session-check can return.
- **FR-016**: This unit MUST NOT implement the functional behavior of any RF01–RF10 requirement; any screen or control belonging to one of them MUST exist only as an inert placeholder, if at all.
- **FR-017**: This unit MUST NOT modify the backend, its contract, or its configuration in any way.

### Key Entities

- **Session**: Represents whether the user is currently authenticated — holds the information needed to stay logged in and to know when it has expired or can be silently renewed. Determines whether a launch routes to Home/Chat or to the login screen, and whether an active screen receives the "Sessão expirada" overlay.
- **Account**: The identity a person signs up with or logs into — an email address and the credential tied to it.
- **Backend Failure**: The error outcome every call introduced by this unit (sign-up, login, refresh, session check) can produce — carries enough information to distinguish a retryable problem from a non-retryable one, and to choose the message shown to the user.
- **Placeholder Destination**: A navigable screen (Meus Registros, Configurações) that exists so later units have somewhere to add their functionality, but carries no behavior of its own in this unit.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: 100% of returning users with a valid stored session reach Home/Chat automatically after the splash state, with no login step required.
- **SC-002**: A new user can go from the sign-up form to a usable Home/Chat screen in a single successful attempt, with no intermediate screen other than the brief splash state.
- **SC-003**: Every error condition that sign-up, login, session-renewal, and session-check can return produces a readable on-screen message rather than a blank screen, a crash, or an indefinite loading state.
- **SC-004**: A user can reach each of the main screens (Home/Chat, Meus Registros, Configurações) from the side menu, and return to Home/Chat, in 2 taps or fewer, every time.
- **SC-005**: When a session expires while a screen is in a particular state, that same state (e.g., scroll position, visible content) is unchanged after the user re-authenticates, in every observed case.
- **SC-006**: Every screen delivered by this unit visually matches the prototype's documented colors, typography, and spacing, with zero visual values defined outside the single central source.

## Assumptions

- Biometric/PIN authentication (RF03) is its own delivery unit, built immediately after this one. Until it exists, the splash state routes directly between itself and the login/sign-up screen — the biometric step shown in the prototype's navigation map is intentionally skipped for this unit and will be inserted by the RF03 unit.
- Re-authenticating from the "Sessão expirada" overlay goes to the login screen (not to a biometric step), for the same reason — RF03 is not yet part of the app.
- Sign-up collects only an email and a password, matching both the prototype (which shows no additional fields) and the backend's sign-up contract.
- Session renewal is attempted silently in the background whenever a request fails because the session has merely expired; the "Sessão expirada" overlay is shown only once silent renewal itself is not possible.
- Where this unit's side menu is shown, "Planos de Ação" may exist as an inert placeholder entry per the product's extension-feature policy, but is not required navigation for this unit — only Home/Chat, Meus Registros, and Configurações are.
- Access and refresh tokens are kept on the device between app launches so a returning user is not asked to log in every time; the specific on-device storage mechanism is an implementation choice, not fixed by this specification.
- Every error this unit's calls (sign-up, login, refresh, session check) can return is one of the backend's fixed, documented error codes; no other error shape is expected from these calls.

37	`docs/input/` are frozen inputs and MUST NOT be edited by anyone working in
38	this repository.
39	
40	Rationale: a reflective-journaling app with a frozen, already-documented
41	backend has exactly one place where ambiguity should be resolved — the
42	product input — so decisions stay traceable and the backend contract stays
43	stable.
44	
45	### II. Fixed Technology Stack
46	The app is built with Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`,
47	using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
48	layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
49	returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
50	text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to
51	the backend. The shipping platform is iOS. Choices not fixed here — routing,
52	HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
53	and charting — are open implementation decisions.
54	
55	Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
56	architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
57	built by different contributors or at different times.
58	
59	### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
60	The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
61	documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
62	(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
63	backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
64	semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
65	NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
66	a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
67	`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
68	carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
69	header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
70	(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
71	marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
72	NEVER be committed.
73	
74	Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
75	scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
76	narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
77	credential leakage.
78	
79	### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity
80	`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
81	spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
82	MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
83	exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
84	documentation MUST be in English.
85	
86	Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
87	checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
88	prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
89	preserving the product's voice.
90	
91	### V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention
92	Code MUST follow the folder convention:
93	```
94	lib/
95	  core/
96	  features/
97	    <feature>/
98	      data/
99	      domain/
100	      presentation/
101	```
102	The domain layer MUST comply with RNF06: zero layer violations — it MUST
103	NOT import `package:flutter` nor any class from a feature's `data/` layer.
104	
105	Rationale: a fixed, enforced folder shape and a flutter/data-free domain
106	layer make the domain independently testable and keep business rules
107	portable regardless of UI or persistence choices.
108	
109	## Quality Standards (RNF01–RNF09)
110	
111	These targets from `docs/input/requirements.md` are binding quality gates:
112	
113	- **RNF01 — Interaction latency**: a local action MUST be reflected in the
114	  UI in under 100 ms; any network call taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a
115	  loading indicator.
116	- **RNF02 — PII stripping**: performed backend-side via Claude Haiku 4.5
117	  with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model; the app
118	  implements no PII-detection logic of its own.
119	- **RNF03 — Zero data retention**: a backend-side policy; the app MUST NOT
120	  introduce its own retention beyond what the backend requires.
121	- **RNF04 — Row Level Security (RLS)**: enforced backend-side; the app MUST
122	  assume RLS is authoritative and MUST NEVER attempt to bypass it.
123	- **RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD)**: the app MUST expose
124	  the account-deletion flow (`DELETE /account`) from Settings.
125	- **RNF06 — Zero layer violations**: see Principle V; 0 violations is the
126	  target.
127	- **RNF07 — Domain test coverage**: `lib/**/domain/**` MUST reach at least

129	- **RNF08 — Visual fidelity**: every screen MUST match the prototype's
130	  color, typography, and spacing, with 0 hardcoded visual values outside
131	  `design_tokens.dart`.
132	- **RNF09 — Consistent network-error handling**: every repository MUST use
133	  the `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart`; every write endpoint (5
134	  endpoints) MUST handle timeout, malformed response, and no-connection
135	  failures, each covered by `mocktail` tests (15 of 15 scenarios).
136

138	
139	- Functional requirements MUST be implemented in the delivery order given in
140	  `docs/input/requirements.md`.
141	- Extension features (section 2 of `requirements.md`) are explicitly out of

1	# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow
2	
3	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.
4	
5	This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Functional requirements
10	
11	### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
12	Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).
13	
14	**Acceptance criteria:**
15	- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
16	- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.
17	
18	### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
19	Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.
22	
23	### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
24	Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.
25	
26	**Acceptance criteria:**
27	- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
28	- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).
29	
30	### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
31	Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.
32	
33	**Acceptance criteria:**
34	- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
35	- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).
36	
37	### RF05 — Personal summary export
38	Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**
39	
40	**Acceptance criteria:**
41	- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
42	- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.
43	
44	### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
45	Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).
46	
47	**Acceptance criteria:**
48	- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
49	- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
50	- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
51	- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
52	- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.
53	
54	### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
55	A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.
56	
57	**Acceptance criteria:**
58	- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
59	- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
60	- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.
61	
62	### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
63	A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**
64	
65	**Acceptance criteria:**
66	- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
67	- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
68	- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.
69	
70	### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
71	An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**
72	
73	**Acceptance criteria:**
74	- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
75	- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
76	- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.
77	
78	### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
79	A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.
80	
81	**Acceptance criteria:**
82	- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
83	- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
84	- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
85	- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 2. Extension features — not implemented
90	
91	They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.
92	
93	| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
94	|---|---|
95	| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
96	| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
97	| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |
98	
99	---
100	
101	## 3. Quality requirements
102	
103	| ID | Requirement | Target |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
106	| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
107	| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
108	| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |
109	
110	## 4. Other non-functional requirements
111	
112	RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).
113	
114	**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.
115	
116	---
117	
118	## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow
119	
120	### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
121	Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.
122	
123	### 5.2 Screens
124	
125	**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*
126	
127	**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*
128	
129	**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*
130	
131	**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*
132	
133	**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*
134	
135	**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*
136	
137	**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*
138	
139	**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 6. Backend endpoint inventory
144	
145	The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.
146	
147	Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.
148	
149	### 6.1 Authentication and session
150	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
151	|---|---|---|
152	| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
153	| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
154	| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
155	| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
156	| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |
157	
158	**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).
159	
160	### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
161	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
164	| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
165	| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
166	| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |
167	
168	**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.
169	
170	### 6.3 Chat and memory (RAG)
171	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
172	|---|---|---|
173	| `POST /chat/sessions` — blocked offline | RF04 | — |
174	| `GET /chat/sessions` — works offline (cache) | RF04, RF07 | — |
175	| `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — works offline (cache) | RF04 | — |
176	| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — streaming (SSE); blocked offline | RF04 | Voyage AI (question embedding) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
177	| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` — regenerates the response without duplicating the user's question; it supports "partial message visible with a failure indication, and a way to try again" in RF04 | RF04 | Voyage AI (embedding, reused from cache) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
178	| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` | RF08 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
179	| `POST /entries` — called from the "save to journal" button (see 6.2) | RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
180	
181	### 6.4 Search
182	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
183	|---|---|---|
184	| `GET /entries/search?q=&source=&dateFrom=&dateTo=&limit=` — no `category` (see RF06) | RF06 | Voyage AI (query embedding) |
185	
186	### 6.5 Export
187	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
188	|---|---|---|
189	| `POST /export/summary` — asynchronous job | RF05 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
190	| `GET /export/:jobId/status` | RF05 | — |
191	| `GET /export/:jobId/download` | RF05 | — |
192	
193	### 6.6 Dashboard
194	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
195	|---|---|---|
196	| `GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=` — separate from the text so it does not block the chart | RF09 | — |
197	| `GET /dashboard/narrative?period=` | RF09 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
198	
199	### 6.7 Account
200	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
201	|---|---|---|
202	| `PATCH /account/settings` — includes the persona toggle (extension) | RNF05, extension | — |
203	| `DELETE /account` | RNF05 | — |
204	
205	---
206	
207	## 7. Integrated flowchart — screens × requirements × backend
208	
209	```mermaid
210	flowchart TD
211	    subgraph T0["Screen 0 — Splash"]
212	        direction TB
213	        E01["GET /auth/session"]
214	    end
215	
216	    subgraph T01["Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault · RF03"]
217	        direction TB
218	        E02b["Face ID / Touch ID / PIN — validated on the device, no backend call"]

# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.

This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).

### RF05 — Personal summary export
Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.

### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.

### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.

---

## 2. Extension features — not implemented

They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.

| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
|---|---|
| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |

---

## 3. Quality requirements

| ID | Requirement | Target |
|---|---|---|
| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |

## 4. Other non-functional requirements

RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).

**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.

---

## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow

### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.

### 5.2 Screens

**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*

**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*

**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*

**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*

**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*

**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*

**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*

**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*

---

## 6. Backend endpoint inventory

The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.

Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.

### 6.1 Authentication and session
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |

**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).

### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |

**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.

### 6.3 Chat and memory (RAG)
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /chat/sessions` — blocked offline | RF04 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions` — works offline (cache) | RF04, RF07 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — works offline (cache) | RF04 | — |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — streaming (SSE); blocked offline | RF04 | Voyage AI (question embedding) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` — regenerates the response without duplicating the user's question; it supports "partial message visible with a failure indication, and a way to try again" in RF04 | RF04 | Voyage AI (embedding, reused from cache) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` | RF08 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `POST /entries` — called from the "save to journal" button (see 6.2) | RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |

### 6.4 Search
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /entries/search?q=&source=&dateFrom=&dateTo=&limit=` — no `category` (see RF06) | RF06 | Voyage AI (query embedding) |

### 6.5 Export
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /export/summary` — asynchronous job | RF05 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `GET /export/:jobId/status` | RF05 | — |
| `GET /export/:jobId/download` | RF05 | — |

### 6.6 Dashboard
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=` — separate from the text so it does not block the chart | RF09 | — |
| `GET /dashboard/narrative?period=` | RF09 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |

### 6.7 Account
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `PATCH /account/settings` — includes the persona toggle (extension) | RNF05, extension | — |
| `DELETE /account` | RNF05 | — |

| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | No connection — action blocked (see RF04/RF06) | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Malformed request body | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | PII check failed before persisting | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | Voyage AI unavailable / error | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | Claude did not respond in time (chat/insight/summary/dashboard) | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist or does not belong to the user | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Request limit exceeded | yes |

The complete, closed list of the backend's 13 codes, with HTTP statuses, is in `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`.

---

## 12. Delivery order

Work is delivered in units, one per functional requirement, preceded by a foundation unit, in this order:

**F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09**

- **F000 (foundation)** covers what no single requirement owns but all of them use: project scaffold, `design_tokens.dart`, HTTP client returning `Either`, login and sign-up (Screen 0.1a in the prototype), base navigation and expired-session handling.
- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.

---

## 13. Technical constraints

**Fixed:**
- Flutter and Dart at the version pinned for the repository (fvm).
- State management: `flutter_bloc`.
- Clean Architecture, three layers per feature.
- Error handling: `fpdart`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`.
- Test doubles: `mocktail`.
- On-device speech-to-text: `whisper_ggml`.
- Visual tokens: `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography, spacing and radii.
- Platform: iOS, portrait only.
- Folder convention:

```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```

**Free (choose what fits):** routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics package, chart package.

1	# Error taxonomy — 13 codes
2	
3	Every endpoint returns errors as `{ code, message, retryable }`. The list below is closed: no other code exists.
4	
5	| Code | HTTP | Retryable |
6	|---|---|---|
7	| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | 401 | no |
8	| `AUTH_INVALID` | 401 | no |
9	| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
10	| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | _(no HTTP response — see note)_ | yes |
11	| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | no |
12	| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
13	| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
14	| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
15	| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | no |
16	| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | yes |
17	| `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` | 400 | no |
18	| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | no |
19	| `OCR_NO_TEXT` | 400 | no |
20	
21	**Two deliberate design choices (these never happen in this API):**
22	- **Never `403`** — a resource belonging to another user always answers `404 NOT_FOUND` (so its existence is not revealed).
23	- **Never `409`** — the idempotency of RF10 (re-sending the same chat message as an entry) always answers `200`; there is no "conflict" code.
24	
25	**`NETWORK_OFFLINE` has no HTTP status:** it is the only code that never becomes an actual response — it represents a connection that ends without any response.
